task:
keep blank-valued query params significant in query_string_matcher

`query_string_matcher` parses both the incoming request query and the configured query with `parse_qsl()` at its default `keep_blank_values=False`, so any empty-valued parameter (`b=`, or a bare `b`) is dropped before comparison:

```python
>>> parse_qsl("a=1&b=")
[('a', '1')]          # b= vanished
```

This matcher is auto-added for any registered URL carrying a query string. As a result `?a=1` matched a request to `?a=1&b=`, and a registration that required `b=` matched a request that omitted it. The request-param parser already uses `keep_blank_values=True`, so `query_param_matcher` treats `b=` as significant — the two query-matching paths disagreed on the same request.

commands: from responses import matchers;from types import SimpleNamespace as R;m=matchers.query_string_matcher('test=1&foo=');assert not m(R(url='http://example.com?test=1'))[0];assert m(R(url='http://example.com?foo=&test=1'))[0];assert not matchers.query_string_matcher('test=1')(R(url='http://example.com?test=1&foo='))[0];assert matchers.query_string_matcher('test=1')(R(url='http://example.com?test=1'))[0];assert matchers.query_string_matcher('')(R(url='http://example.com'))[0]
